examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'личный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('excellent').

examples.text: Квартира будет отличная. На Симашко есть новый дом.
examples.trans: It'll be an excellent flat. There's a new building on Simashko Street.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

examples.text: Это правильно. Я приглашаю вас в общественный совет.
examples.trans: That's right. I'm inviting you onto the public council.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.
The chef wants to surprise the restaurant guests.

examples.text: Ты должен очень сильно удивить наших гостей.
examples.trans: You must greatly surprise our guests.
Now I will surprise you all!

meanings.note: + genitive: ни копейки = not a penny

examples.text: Пятьсот. А у меня ни копейки.
examples.trans: Five hundred. And I haven't got a penny.

meanings.note: agrees in gender and case with the noun

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

examples.text: Главное в нашем деле — умение работать с документами.
examples.trans: The main thing in our work is knowing how to work with documents.

meanings.en: to get used to, become accustomed
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'выкнуть'). Used as an verbal verb meaning 'to get used to'.

examples.text: Я ещё не привык к Москве.
examples.trans: I am not used to Moscow yet.

examples.text: Ты уже привык к жизни в Москве?
examples.trans: Have you already gotten used to life in Moscow?
I got used to working by the law.

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

examples.text: Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
examples.trans: It's Arakelyan. I'm calling about the shopping centre.
This is the law of the country.

examples.text: Я помню все установленные законом правила.
examples.trans: I remember all the rules established by law.

meanings.note: очень приятно = pleased to meet you

examples.text: Очень приятно. А в чём дело?
examples.trans: Pleased to meet you. So what's the matter?
Can I go and have a look?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('other, another, different').

examples.text: Послушайте, а можно в другое место? Здесь плохо пахнет.
examples.trans: Listen, could we go somewhere else? It smells bad in here.
There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: used as an exclamation of approval

examples.trans: I know this town really well!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to love, to like', paired with 'полюбить'.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('French').

examples.trans: And you're drinking French cognac yourself.
Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.
There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: to run for a second term

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'верка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'check, inspection, test' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: An inspection is underway at the bank.

examples.text: Эксперты уже начали проверку состояния старой стены.
examples.trans: Experts have already begun checking the condition of the old wall.

meanings.note: pointing at something a little way off
вон отсюда! = get out of here!
